articles.title: Washington governor Bob Ferguson says ICE is 'out of control' & 'deeply un-American' after airport arrest
articles.summary: Governor Bob Ferguson criticizes ICE for chaotic airport arrests that raised concerns about public safety and civil rights, as federal agents detain passengers during boarding.
articles.body: Washington Governor Bob Ferguson has accused US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) of using "deeply un-American" tactics after federal agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle, triggering a confrontation with passengers boarding a flight to Los Angeles.Ferguson criticised the operation at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday, alleging that masked officers had created chaos by removing passengers during the boarding process. He said the incident raised concerns about how federal immigration enforcement was being conducted in public spaces."ICE is completely and totally out of control," Ferguson wrote on X. "Like many Americans, I'm outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities."The arrests took place at around 8.05am local time on Alaska Airlines Flight 1306's jet bridge, shortly before the aircraft was scheduled to depart for Los Angeles. ICE said the operation targeted Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who allegedly remained in the United States after his visa expired.Federal agents also detained another passenger, identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia. According to ICE, she had also overstayed her visa and threw hot coffee at officers during the operation. The agency said she could face charges of assaulting a federal officer and warned that anyone interfering with law enforcement would face prosecution.Footage of the incident circulating online showed masked officers pulling people away from the boarding area as other passengers watched. A woman could be heard shouting that her daughter was being detained and had a work permit. Officers were also seen struggling with an individual on the floor.The airport operation also drew criticism from Alaska Airlines, which said it had received no advance notification of the enforcement action. The airline expressed concern about the arrests taking place while passengers were boarding its aircraft."We are concerned by this morning's law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306," the airline said in a statement.It added that the incident had caused distress among passengers and employees and that it was working with the Port of Seattle to determine whether established procedures had been followed. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday upped the ante against BJP and RSS, calling them "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists" and accusing them of having no understanding of India's spiritual and religious traditions."The deeper I go into Indian spiritual and religious traditions, the clearer it becomes," the Congress leader wrote in a social media post on X."The BJP and RSS are uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists with absolutely no understanding of our spiritual and religious traditions," he added.The Congress leader also shared a picture of a sculpture depicting Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati in the form of 'Ardhanareshwar'. Ardhanareshwar is a Hindu deity representing Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati in a single form, with one half depicting a male and the other a female.Rahul's remarks come days after he faced criticism over his comments about his parents' relationship at the launch of his mother Sonia Gandhi's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love'.Recalling his childhood, he said his parents would sit together during meals, with his mother sitting on his father's lap."Now, I thought this was a normal thing. So I would go to my friend's house, but their parents wouldn't be sitting on each other's lap, and I'd ask my friends, 'Guys, what is going on? Why is your mother not sitting on your father's lap?'" he said."... And then we saw it all get smashed. Not just over time - suddenly... We saw one of our anchors (Indira Gandhi) get shot, and then we saw our biggest anchor (Rajiv) get blown to pieces," he added.The remarks drew criticism from BJP leaders, including Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who took a swipe at the Congress leader."Sorry, Ma'am, he couldn't spare you the embarrassment even on such a special day of your life. The nation figured it out long ago. Hopefully you'll see it now too; this product is beyond launching and relaunching," Sarma said in a post on X, sharing a video of Rahul's remarks.The Congress leader countered saying thar fear, anger and hatred had created a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters, preventing them from expressing love.He had also shared a photograph of a 12th-century temple sculpture depicting Goddess Parvati sitting on Lord Shiva's lap."As a true Hindu, it is my duty to free them from this web, so that they too can start to experience the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging in their lives. articles.body: Indonesian police recovered seven body bags after a massive fire broke out at a factory in western Java, while rescue teams continued searching for around 50 missing workers on Sunday. Firefighters were still battling hotspots more than a day after the blaze started.According to news agency Reuters, police said some of the recovered body bags could contain remains belonging to multiple victims.Authorities said the intensity of the fire had made it impossible to identify the victims through visual examination. They are now collecting DNA samples from relatives of missing workers and gathering their personal belongings to establish their identities."Seven body bags have been recovered," said Wahyu Hidayati, a police official involved in disaster victim identification. She added that the victims could not be identified through visual inspection because of the severity of the fire.Hidayati said the blaze had not been completely extinguished and the identification process could take between two and three weeks.As part of the identification efforts, authorities are collecting DNA samples from family members of missing workers. They are also gathering personal belongings from the workers' homes and dormitories to help identify the victims.The factory owner said at a news conference that around 300 workers were present during the shift when the fire broke out. He clarified that the figure of 50 referred to workers whose whereabouts had not yet been established.The fire broke out on Saturday evening at a candy factory in Cikande, located in Serang regency. Authorities are investigating the cause of the blaze.Rescue teams were searching through sections of the damaged factory where workers were believed to be trapped. An official warned that some parts of the building remained at risk of collapsing.The factory belongs to Indonesia's united Family Food company, which was established in 1981, according to its website.The company manufactures consumer goods across Indonesia, employs around 5,000 people and operates from its national headquarters and four international offices. articles.title: China’s secret AI chip hunt: How its spyverse is helping firms bypass US curbs
articles.summary: China’s race to catch up with the US in artificial intelligence is not just playing out in laboratories and boardrooms.
articles.body: China’s race to catch up with the US in artificial intelligence is not just playing out in laboratories and boardrooms. Its intelligence agency has also been drawn into the effort, running a secret campaign to help Chinese companies obtain advanced AI chips that Washington has barred them from buying, according to The New York Times.The campaign, which has been underway for at least two years, involves efforts to acquire and smuggle restricted semiconductors into China, while gathering intelligence on the chip industry and its supply chains, the NYT reported, citing serving and former security and intelligence officials.The Ministry of State Security (MSS), China’s principal civilian intelligence agency, has made acquiring advanced chips and intelligence on the sector a priority, the report said. The effort includes helping Chinese companies obtain and smuggle restricted semiconductors into the country, as well as collecting information about the industry and its supply chains.The campaign is being led by a working group established by MSS chief Chen Yixin, which reports directly to him. The group was tasked with supporting China’s efforts to counter Western export restrictions.Chen outlined the agency’s expanded mission in April, calling for a deeper “struggle against blockades” and greater progress in artificial intelligence innovation and industrial development.“Focus on tackling the ‘chokeholds’ of critical technologies,” Chen wrote in a Communist Party journal, according to the investigation, referring to technologies China cannot obtain through ordinary commercial channels.China’s push to overcome US chip restrictionsThe intelligence campaign is part of a broader strategy under Chinese president Xi Jinping to reduce China’s dependence on foreign technology and close its gap with the US in computing power.Xi has urged officials to take extraordinary measures to acquire core technologies in sectors considered vital to China’s future. In a January speech to the Politburo, he called for resolving technological bottlenecks that were holding back the development of emerging industries.The US began restricting exports of advanced Nvidia chips to China in late 2022, citing concerns that the technology could help Beijing break American encryption systems and develop new weapons.China’s wider technology drive is coordinated by the Central Science and Technology Commission, a Communist Party body established by Xi in 2023. The commission is led by Ding Xuexiang, a member of the party’s top leadership and a vice premier overseeing science and technology policy.The NYT reported that the commission works to mobilise scientists, research institutions, laboratories and companies around national priorities, including technological self-reliance.“Computing power is a major indicator of overall national power,” Ding said in May, according to China’s official Xinhua news agency.Alice Huang case and the Nvidia scandal raises suspicionThe campaign has come under scrutiny as the US investigates Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom American officials allege was working with China’s intelligence agency to gather information about Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang.The allegations were first reported by The New York Times. China has dismissed the espionage claims as “pure fabrication”.The precise nature of her role in the intelligence agency’s chip effort remains unclear. US officials allege that she passed information about Jensen Huang to Beijing and that her company, Megaspeed, was involved in the illegal smuggling of advanced chips into China.Megaspeed, based in Singapore, purchased billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips and provided high-end computing services to Chinese companies. The arrangement allowed firms in China to access Nvidia technology through data centres located outside the country, potentially bypassing restrictions on direct sales.The NYT also reported last week that Megaspeed may have been helping a research laboratory with links to China’s military through Alibaba, the Chinese internet company that is both a customer and financial backer of Megaspeed.Alibaba denied the allegation.The report also cited Alex Joske, managing director of Garnaut Global, a consultancy that studies China’s security apparatus, who said China’s intelligence agency was comfortable using commercial and research networks to gather information.“MSS is very comfortable using business covers,” Joske said, adding that it could run people as intelligence assets “without directly telling those people that they’re working for the MSS.”US moves to close overseas data centre loopholeThe Trump administration announced on Monday that it would introduce new restrictions aimed at preventing Chinese companies from accessing advanced American chips through overseas data centres.Under the proposed rule, data centres outside China would need a government licence before providing significant computing power to companies headquartered in countries including China, Russia and Iran. The restriction is expected to take effect in about 90 days.The move could further intensify Beijing’s push to develop its own advanced semiconductor capabilities and reduce reliance on Western technology.Xi has framed technological self-reliance as a national priority.You use AI every day. articles.title: The US tech slump: FBI breach, corporate outages expose vulnerabilities in America's digital systems
articles.summary: From a suspected breach of the FBI's crime database to outages affecting Microsoft, Amazon Web Services and the Federal Aviation Administration, a series
articles.body: From a suspected breach of the FBI's crime database to outages affecting Microsoft, Amazon Web Services and the Federal Aviation Administration, a series of back-to-back incidents has put America's digital infrastructure under scrutiny. While the disruptions have different causes, they raise questions about software vulnerabilities, third-party risks and the resilience of systems powering government agencies and private companies.The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating a suspected breach of its National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a sensitive database used by law enforcement agencies across the United States. The suspected breach has raised fresh concerns about government cybersecurity, coming amid reports of a separate intrusion involving a US Department of Agriculture (USDA) system used for farmer payments.The NCIC contains information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. The extent of the suspected breach, the information potentially accessed and the identity of those responsible remain unclear.President Donald Trump, responding to the report, said: “We just heard about it and I will say that it’s not good.”The FBI incident comes amid a series of technology disruptions affecting major US organisations. Microsoft 365, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Amazon Web Services (AWS) and the National Security Agency (NSA) have all faced outages or network problems in November. JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have also disclosed a cyber incident involving a third-party service provider.These incidents do not point to one coordinated cyberattack. Some involved suspected unauthorised access, while others resulted from software defects, network failures or maintenance-related problems. But together, they expose a common challenge: America's growing dependence on interconnected digital systems, where a failure in one component can affect services far beyond the organisation directly involved.FBI and USDA incidents raise concerns over government dataThe suspected NCIC breach has added to scrutiny of the FBI's cybersecurity arrangements. In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have compromised the bureau's recruitment website. In March, the FBI disclosed suspicious activity involving an internal system containing sensitive surveillance and law-enforcement information.The USDA has also been dealing with a reported cybersecurity incident. The department's security operations centre reportedly identified an intrusion that led IT staff to take multiple applications offline and reset database passwords.The disruption affected financial tools used to facilitate payments to farmers, including programmes linked to crop insurance and agricultural losses. The identity of the attackers and whether information was stolen had not been established in the reporting discussed.These cases highlight the risks associated with government databases containing sensitive personal, financial and law-enforcement information. However, the distinction between an attempted intrusion, a confirmed breach and actual data theft remains important. The full scope of the FBI and USDA incidents is still unclear.November's outage cluster: Microsoft, FAA, AWS and NSAThe Microsoft 365 outage, which began on November 12, affected services including Outlook, Teams and Exchange Online. Microsoft's post-incident explanation pointed to a combination of a latent software defect, increased network traffic and reduced server capacity.A software change introduced in July had created a defect in the company's gateway infrastructure. The issue remained undetected until Teams traffic was shifted from an alternate gateway to a primary gateway also handling Exchange Online.The primary system was already operating with nearly 14% less capacity than normal. As servers became unresponsive, traffic was redirected to the remaining infrastructure, increasing pressure on it. At the peak, more than 80% of the affected gateway servers were reportedly unresponsive.Microsoft applied fixes and restored services by November 13. The company said there was no evidence of malicious activity.The incident showed how a dormant software defect can trigger a wider failure when combined with increased traffic and insufficient backup capacity.The FAA faced a different problem on November 13. A network disruption linked to a router installation at a communications facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, forced the agency to issue a nationwide ground stop.The installation was part of an upgrade to replace older copper-line equipment with fibre-linked systems. Officials said the network experienced an abnormal volume of connection attempts, reportedly around 1,000 every four to five seconds. The disruption affected communications and radar data feeds at 17 of the FAA's 22 en-route air traffic control centres.The agency halted departures as a precaution. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours, while Reuters reported more than 18,000 flight cancellations over the following days. The FAA suspended further deployment of the routers while it investigated the incident. Officials said they had no indication of a cyberattack, and the precise technical cause remained under investigation.On November 15, AWS reported connectivity and authentication problems in its US-East-1 region in Northern Virginia. The disruption affected several cloud services, with most restored within hours.Other companies also reported problems. JPMorgan Chase experienced a transaction-processing failure on November 16 attributed to a software bug. United Airlines reported flight delays linked to a system problem, while Apple services and Marriott's website and app also faced disruptions.The NSA's internal classified network, NSANet, experienced a disruption during maintenance and software patching. Officials indicated that patches applied after a PHP vulnerability alert caused some systems not to restart as expected. The disruption lasted several days, but officials said mission-critical intelligence operations continued.The incidents had different technical causes. They nevertheless demonstrate how software defects, network equipment, maintenance and capacity constraints can disrupt essential services even without a malicious attack.When a trusted digital certificate is not secureBeyond network failures, cybersecurity researchers are warning about weaknesses in the systems organisations use to establish digital trust.Digital certificates verify the identity of websites, software publishers and online services. They rely on cryptographic keys, including private keys. If a private key is generated using a flawed process, a certificate may appear legitimate even though its underlying security is compromised.The issue has come into focus following concerns around private key generation involving eMudhra, a certificate authority.Saurabh Sharma, Lead Security Researcher at Kaspersky's Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT), said conventional security tools may fail to identify weaknesses in the way cryptographic keys are generated.“A certificate can pass every standard check and still not be safe to trust. In our DAEMON Tools investigation, trojanized installers carried a valid digital signature from the developer and came from the official website, so signature checks alone raised no alarm. Most security tools watch traffic and code, so a weakness in how a key was generated stays just as invisible.”Sharma said organisations should monitor certificate transparency logs, independently test public keys for weak patterns and examine how certificate authorities audit key generation. Shorter certificate lifespans can also reduce the period during which a flawed key can be misused.Another problem arises when certificates are revoked or no longer trusted by browsers, but backend systems continue using outdated trust lists.“Browsers get fixed quickly, while backend systems are often forgotten,” Sharma said.He cited Kaspersky's research into container security, which found critical vulnerabilities in 64 of 100 popular Docker Hub images sampled. Only one in ten was fully up to date.“Pre-built images do not patch themselves. They must be rebuilt and redeployed by hand, and the same applies to any trust list baked into them. Organisations should list every trust store in use across operating systems, runtimes, base images and bundled libraries, rebuild images on a fixed schedule and treat trust store updates like critical patches.”The concern is that organisations may update their main applications while overlooking outdated software components, libraries and certificate stores embedded in their systems.PHP2Shell and the shrinking window to patch vulnerabilitiesThe speed at which vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited is creating another challenge for security teams.The PHP2Shell vulnerability has raised questions about protecting web servers against flaws that can be triggered before application-level security controls come into play.A web application firewall (WAF) can block known malicious request patterns, but it cannot replace a security patch. It must also distinguish malicious traffic from legitimate requests, particularly when websites handle large file uploads.Sharma said organisations need a layered approach.“A flaw that triggers before application code runs leaves a firewall little to work with, but not nothing. Our Q4 2025 report on exploits and vulnerabilities shows that several flaws were exploited in the wild almost immediately after publication, so speed matters.”He recommended virtual patching rules, strict limits on request structures and rate limiting. Upload endpoints should have separate size thresholds to avoid blocking legitimate large files.However, these measures only buy time. “A firewall buys time, and patching remains the fix,” Sharma said.The challenge becomes more serious when vulnerability information or software patches become public. Attackers can analyse code changes to understand what has been fixed and develop exploits before all organisations have updated their systems.“The clock starts for attackers the moment a fix becomes public. As our Q2 2026 report on exploits and vulnerabilities notes, early publication of exploits gives attackers an advantage, leaving developers with little or no time to fix the issue.”Sharma said organisations should reduce the exposure of internet-facing systems, use behavioural detection to identify exploitation attempts and prioritise assets that are most vulnerable.Software supply chains: When clean source code does not mean safe softwareThe LiteLLM incident has drawn attention to another weakness: the gap between open-source code available for inspection and the actual software packages that companies download and run.While the official GitHub repository reportedly contained clean code, malicious versions were pushed directly to package repositories, including PyPI and Docker. Users downloading affected packages could therefore be exposed even if they relied on the project's public source code.Sharma said organisations must verify the software they install rather than assume that clean source code guarantees safety.“Clean source code says nothing about the package that is actually installed. Our OceanLotus research found malicious packages sitting on PyPI since July 2025, and our report on open-source threats recorded a 48% increase in malicious packages by the end of 2024.”He recommended monitoring open-source repositories, checking package names and versions against known threats, pinning software versions and verifying package hashes. Organisations can also use vetted internal repositories to reduce the risk of downloading compromised packages.The problem is particularly relevant to companies building applications using multiple third-party libraries and tools. A malicious dependency can provide attackers with access to systems that are otherwise protected.AI is accelerating vulnerability discoveryArtificial intelligence is adding another dimension to the cybersecurity challenge. AI tools can analyse large codebases and identify weaknesses that may have remained undetected for years. But attackers can use similar capabilities to automate reconnaissance and search for exploitable flaws.Sharma said both attackers and defenders are increasingly using the same discovery tools.“Defenders and attackers now use the same discovery tools, and the volume shows it. Our Q2 2026 report records an unprecedented number of registered CVEs, driven largely by AI-assisted discovery in third-party software.”He cautioned that older vulnerabilities remain a major threat, even as new flaws are identified.“Veteran vulnerabilities such as CVE-2018-0802 remain among the exploits our solutions detect most often, and ToolShell in SharePoint traced back to an incomplete fix from 2020. Flaws in AI services are rising too, with a tenfold increase between Q4 2025 and Q2 2026.”The persistence of older vulnerabilities suggests that the problem is not just the discovery of new flaws. Organisations often struggle to identify outdated systems, assess which vulnerabilities are actively exploited and deploy fixes across their infrastructure.Sharma said defenders need to prioritise exposed and actively exploited vulnerabilities, while using tools that can detect exploitation behaviour even when a patch is unavailable.Are compliance certificates enough to establish security?The growing dependence on third-party providers has also raised questions about the reliability of compliance certifications and security audits.A vendor may meet the requirements of an audit at a particular point in time but remain vulnerable to a newly discovered flaw or a compromised software dependency.Sharma said organisations should not treat compliance certification as proof that a product is secure.“A compliance certificate is a baseline, not proof of security. It shows that a process existed on the audit date, not that the product holds up against a live attacker.”He said enterprise security teams should ask vendors for penetration-test results, software bills of materials, vulnerability disclosure records and evidence of secure software development. Contracts should also include audit rights, alongside continuous monitoring after a vendor has been onboarded.The November cyber incident involving JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard illustrates the risks. The reported attack involved a third-party service provider, rather than a confirmed compromise of the companies' core payment networks. It shows how information can be exposed through an external partner even when an organisation's primary systems remain operational.A resilience test for America's digital infrastructureThe November incidents do not establish that America's digital infrastructure is collapsing or that a single adversary is behind the disruptions. But they expose how dependence on interconnected systems can turn relatively contained problems into wider operational crises.The FAA incident demonstrated the challenges of introducing new equipment into legacy infrastructure. Microsoft's outage showed how a software defect and capacity constraints can overwhelm systems designed to provide redundancy. The suspected FBI and USDA intrusions, meanwhile, have raised questions about protecting sensitive government information.The risks extend beyond software and cybersecurity. Data centres depend on uninterrupted electricity, cooling and network connectivity. Microsoft's Azure infrastructure experienced a major power and cooling-related incident in May 2026, underlining how physical infrastructure failures can also disrupt digital services.The response requires more than investing in new technology. Organisations need independently tested backup systems, accurate inventories of software and internet-facing assets, stronger third-party security checks and reliable patch-management procedures.The central lesson is that technological sophistication does not automatically translate into resilience. As AI accelerates vulnerability discovery and software supply chains become more complex, the challenge for the US government and private companies is to ensure that their systems can withstand an intrusion, a software failure or a compromised component without disrupting essential services.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'I want a Brezza': Bride's family gifts Delhi cop Hyundai Aura, he calls it a 'taxi', leaves her waiting at mandap
articles.summary: SONIPAT: A wedding in Sonipat turned into a controversy after a Delhi Police personnel allegedly refused to proceed with the marriage over a dispute
articles.body: SONIPAT: A wedding in Sonipat turned into a controversy after a Delhi Police personnel allegedly refused to proceed with the marriage over a dispute concerning the car arranged by the bride’s family.The groom, Kuldeep, allegedly insisted on a Maruti Suzuki Brezza instead of the Hyundai Aura booked by the bride’s family, reportedly describing the latter as a vehicle commonly used as a taxi.Following the disagreement, he returned with around 30 members of the wedding party, leaving the bride waiting at the mandap in her wedding attire.According to a complaint filed by the bride’s father, Subhash Kumar, a resident of the Ram Nagar area, his daughter Hina’s marriage had been fixed with Kuldeep, a resident of Gandhi Nagar in Gohana, around six months ago.Both families had mutually agreed to solemnise the marriage on November 20, following which the family began preparations and sent invitations to relatives.Subhash alleged that the issue of a car came up on November 19, a day before the wedding. His family was scheduled to visit the groom’s house for the engagement ceremony. Before the visit, he received a phone call from Anil and Rajesh, who had helped arrange the marriage.During the conversation, Anil allegedly asked whether the bride’s family had arranged a car for the wedding. Subhash said he had already booked a vehicle for the groom.However, Anil subsequently informed him that Kuldeep was not satisfied with the Hyundai Aura booked for him. The groom allegedly said that the model was commonly used as a taxi and that he wanted a Brezza instead.The bride’s father claimed that he cancelled the booking of the Aura, which was worth approximately Rs 9.5 lakh, and approached several dealers in Sonipat and nearby areas to arrange a Brezza. However, with very little time left before the wedding, he could not arrange the vehicle. He also claimed that the groom’s family later spoke about arranging a car from Narnaund.In his complaint, Subhash alleged that his family had made arrangements to gift Kuldeep a two-tola gold chain, his mother four-tola gold earrings and a silver anklet. Jewellery was also planned for the groom’s elder brother and sister-in-law.Besides this, good-quality furniture and other household items had been prepared for the groom, involving an expenditure of around Rs 1.32 lakh.The family had booked Mamchand Vatika for the wedding and arranged food for approximately 1,200 guests. Subhash claimed that the family had spent between Rs 25 lakh and Rs 30 lakh on the wedding preparations.According to the complainant, on November 20, when the Brezza could not be arranged, Kuldeep arrived at the wedding venue in ordinary clothes along with his mother instead of proceeding with the customary wedding ceremonies.Subhash alleged that members of the groom’s family abused the bride’s relatives. He further claimed that Kuldeep’s sister-in-law, while identifying herself as an advocate, threatened to take them to court. Kuldeep allegedly invoked his position in Delhi Police during the confrontation.Following the altercation, the groom left the venue with around 30 members of the wedding party. The incident left Hina waiting at the mandap in her bridal attire as the marriage ceremony remained incomplete.Subhash said his daughter Hina had completed her MA and JBT qualifications, while Kuldeep had studied up to Class XII. He alleged that at the time of finalising the alliance, the groom’s family had assured them that they would neither make any demands nor accept dowry. However, demands concerning a car and jewellery allegedly surfaced around the wedding.After the baraat left, Subhash called the emergency helpline 112 to inform the police. The groom’s side also reportedly contacted the helpline. Subsequently, the bride’s family approached Sector 27 police station and submitted a complaint seeking action against Kuldeep and his family.Sector 27 police station SHO Savit Kumar said the police had received a complaint from the bride’s family and had called both parties to the police station.“Both parties have been called, and discussions are currently underway. articles.title: A basset hound named Becky arrived alone at a New York mountain lodge after her 69-year-old owner went missing; staff recognised the dog and alerted rescuers, who found the man alive after a freezing night outdoors
articles.summary: A missing person’s search in New York’s Adirondack Mountains took an unexpected turn when a familiar four-legged visitor arrived at a mountain lodge
articles.body: A missing person’s search in New York’s Adirondack Mountains took an unexpected turn when a familiar four-legged visitor arrived at a mountain lodge without her owner. Becky, a basset hound, turned up alone at the Whiteface Mountain lodge on November 12, prompting staff members to contact authorities. Their quick recognition of the dog eventually helped rescuers locate her 69-year-old owner, who had spent the night outdoors in freezing temperatures. The incident was reported by WRGB CBS 6 News, Popular Science and ABC7 New York, drawing attention to the unusual role the dog played in the rescue. According to the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC), Becky arrived at the lodge in Wilmington, Essex County, at around 9 pm. Staff members immediately recognised her and knew that her owner, who has dementia, had gone missing on previous occasions.Concerned by her unexpected appearance without him, the staff contacted New York State Police. Officers began looking for the missing man and subsequently requested assistance from DEC Forest Rangers. The initial search involved four forest rangers and state police personnel, who used a drone and a bloodhound to cover the surrounding terrain. As the hours passed without finding the man, the operation expanded to include 14 forest rangers, four state police members and the New York State Police Aviation Unit.A hunter finally spots the missing manThe search continued through the night as temperatures dropped below freezing. According to Popular Science, conditions were particularly harsh, with temperatures ranging between 25 and 30 degrees Fahrenheit. At around 10 am the following morning, a hunter searching ahead of the rescue team heard someone fall and call out for help. He located the missing man in a wooded drainage area, away from the trail, and alerted the authorities. Forest Ranger Sabo reached the location within minutes. The 69-year-old was found without shoes or gloves and was suffering from severe frostbite to his hands and feet. Despite spending several hours exposed to the cold, he was still conscious and able to communicate with rescuers.Given the man’s injuries and the difficult terrain, rescuers decided that carrying him out on foot would not be the safest option. Instead, they arranged an aerial evacuation. Forest Ranger Martin operated the helicopter hoist, lifting the man from the remote location into the aircraft. New York State Police Pilot Engel then transported him to a hospital for medical treatment. The rescue operation was officially completed at 11.50 am.How Becky’s arrival changed the searchWhile the rescue involved a coordinated effort by forest rangers, police officers, aviation personnel and a hunter, officials credited Becky with helping bring attention to the man’s disappearance before the situation became even more dangerous. Charlie Foutch, the lead forest ranger involved in the operation, said the dog’s unexpected arrival had made it possible for authorities to begin searching sooner. Without that early alert, locating the missing man could have taken considerably longer, potentially leaving him exposed to another night in the freezing conditions.The incident also highlighted how familiar animals can sometimes become an important link in recognising that something is wrong, particularly when their owners are vulnerable or unable to seek assistance themselves. Becky’s appearance at the lodge ultimately set a chain of events in motion that brought multiple emergency teams together and helped reunite a missing man with his rescuers. What began as an unusual sighting of a familiar dog ended with a successful mountain rescue, with Becky playing an unexpected but significant part in bringing her owner home.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1981, Bea Gaddy began feeding neighbours in Baltimore on Thanksgiving; 45 years later, her daughter had only eight turkeys for thousands until chef Jose Andres and Maryland prison workers stepped in to help
articles.summary: With Thanksgiving approaching, Cynthia Brooks was facing the possibility of cancelling a food drive that has been part of Baltimore's community life for
articles.body: With Thanksgiving approaching, Cynthia Brooks was facing the possibility of cancelling a food drive that has been part of Baltimore's community life for 45 years. The daughter of the late Bea Gaddy had only eight turkeys and limited supplies for an event meant to provide meals to people in need. Help arrived after celebrity chef Jose Andres and Maryland correctional services stepped in with food and other support, CBS News reported.The shortage was particularly difficult for Brooks because the annual dinner carries on work started by her mother in 1981. Gaddy had begun by preparing Thanksgiving meals at her home. Over the years, the effort grew into a community event, and Brooks took responsibility for continuing it. This year's preparations, however, were far from complete just days before the holiday.Brooks said donations had been slower than usual as families and businesses dealt with a difficult economic situation. The lack of supplies left her uncertain about whether she could organise the event at all. She appealed for public support, hoping that enough people and organisations would come forward to keep the tradition going.The response eventually came from several quarters. Andres offered help through his organisations, while the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services arranged a large turkey donation. The contributions helped address the shortage and allowed preparations for the Thanksgiving meal to move forward.Jose Andres offers support after appealThe scale of the shortage became clear earlier in the week when Brooks spoke to WBAL-TV. The organisation had only 30 cans of string beans, 18 cans of corn and eight turkeys on Monday, despite having plans to provide meals to hundreds of people.According to the report, the original plan was to deliver food to as many as 500 people and host approximately 300 people for a sit-down Thanksgiving dinner. With so few supplies available, Brooks was struggling to see how the event could go ahead.The report caught the attention of Andres, who sharednthe coverage on social media and offered assistance. He said his organisations would work with the family services centre to make sure people received food.In his post on X, Andres wrote: "Tell them food will be in their way…we will contact them and help them and Longer Tables Fund will take care of it with the help of World Central Kitchen #BaltimoreStrong."The offer came through World Central Kitchen and the Longer Tables Fund. Brooks was surprised when she learnt about the sponsorship. Speaking to WBAL-TV, she reacted by saying, "What? I'm here screaming."She contacted the station again within an hour to confirm that the organisation had reached out to her. She was told that the entire meal would receive sponsorship, giving the organisers much-needed support at a critical stage of the preparations.World Central Kitchen was founded by Andres and works to provide meals during emergencies and crises. Its approach involves using available local resources and responding quickly to the food requirements of affected communities.Maryland correctional facility contributes hundreds of turkeysThe assistance was not limited to Andres' organisations. Maryland's Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services also contributed hundreds of turkeys for the Thanksgiving event.The birds were prepared by incarcerated individuals working at the Maryland Correctional Enterprises Meat Plant. The donation provided a substantial amount of the food needed for the event, which had been struggling to secure even basic supplies.Andres' team also agreed to prepare several dishes for the gathering. These included string beans, corn, sweet potatoes and stuffing. The contribution meant that the organisers would receive help with both the main food item and the accompanying dishes.Brooks said the support would make a significant difference to the meal. "They're preparing all the sides, the string beans, the corn, the sweet potatoes for the dinner, the stuffing for the dinner. It's going to be a great, great contribution to the meal," she told CBS News.For Brooks, the response also brought back the purpose behind her mother's work. She said the support reflected the willingness of people in Baltimore and Maryland to help others, even when the city faced its own difficulties."This city, with all of its faults and all of its things, it's a beautiful city. The spirit of our city is everything. It was that to her, and it's that to me," she said.She also spoke about her pride in the community's response. "It's makes me feel good. I'm so proud of the spirit of Baltimore, the spirit of Maryland. I'm so proud to be a Marylander," Brooks said.How the Thanksgiving dinner began in 1981The annual meal traces its beginnings to Bea Gaddy, who started serving Thanksgiving food from her home in 1981. Her initiative eventually became a long-running community tradition, with her daughter continuing the work after her death.The Bea Gaddy Family Center now provides food, clothing and essential household items to individuals and families across the Greater Baltimore metropolitan area and other parts of Maryland.The centre's Thanksgiving programme is one part of this work. Its aim is to ensure that people who need assistance can access a holiday meal, whether through food deliveries or a community gathering.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2018, Carolyn Marshall began preparing 22 turkeys and 700 Christmas dinners using just one oven; carrying forward her mother’s legacy, she continued feeding hundreds of people who might otherwise go without a holiday meal
articles.summary: For Carolyn Marshall, Christmas has always been about more than celebrations at home.
articles.body: For Carolyn Marshall, Christmas has always been about more than celebrations at home. Every year, she takes on an enormous cooking operation to ensure that people facing financial hardship, older residents and those without a festive meal can still enjoy a traditional Christmas dinner. In 2018, her remarkable effort was documented by The Washington Post’s Jessica Contrera and The Lily, while a subsequent report by Voice of America offered a glimpse into how her family’s charitable work continued. At the centre of the operation was Marshall’s home in Washington, DC, where she prepared an estimated 700 meals using a single oven. The menu included 22 turkeys weighing approximately 460 pounds in total, along with stuffing, sweet potatoes, green beans and gravy.While volunteers helped pack the food into individual containers and deliver it across the city, the cooking was largely Marshall’s responsibility. She managed the preparation herself, balancing the work with her regular job as a teaching assistant. Her efforts were not limited to Christmas. She also organised meals for people in need during Thanksgiving, making the holiday season an especially demanding period for her and the volunteers who supported the initiative.A mother’s legacy that became a family traditionMarshall’s commitment to feeding people in need came from her mother, the Reverend Annie Woodridge, who was affectionately known as Mother Dear. Woodridge established a charitable organisation in 1957, building a reputation as a community organiser and advocate for people who often had nowhere else to turn. Her work extended well beyond providing food. She organised after-school programmes and summer camps for children, helped unemployed people prepare their resumes and supported formerly incarcerated individuals as they tried to rebuild their lives.She also regularly served meals to homeless residents, becoming a familiar and respected presence in the Washington community. After Woodridge died in 1987, her daughters continued the work she had started, keeping the holiday meal tradition alive through the family organisation.However, the initiative faced a major setback in 2010 when the family lost the building that housed its community centre amid redevelopment and rising property costs. Despite attempts to find another affordable location, Marshall and her sister Iris were unable to secure a suitable space.The family eventually had to pause its holiday meal programme for a year. But requests for food continued to come in, prompting Marshall to find another way to serve the community. She decided to move the operation into her own home, turning her kitchen into a makeshift food preparation centre.The enormous effort behind 700 mealsPreparing hundreds of dinners required months of planning, careful budgeting and considerable physical effort. Marshall typically began organising the Christmas operation in September, contacting previous donors and coordinating with local social service agencies to identify people who needed meals.The shopping alone was a substantial undertaking. She purchased supplies in bulk from warehouse stores, using a shopping cart and a flatbed trolley to transport the ingredients. Her list included dozens of large cans of vegetables, cranberry sauce, milk, cheese, butter and more than 100 boxes of stuffing mix.The food preparation continued late into Christmas Eve. Marshall cooked the different dishes in batches, carefully managing the limited oven space and preparing the meals for volunteers to package. By Christmas morning, the kitchen became a distribution centre. Volunteers wore gloves, aprons and hairnets as they divided the food into individual containers.Drivers were assigned delivery routes, with meals taken to elderly residents, people living alone and families who might otherwise have gone without a proper Christmas dinner. The initiative also made room for unexpected recipients. Drivers were encouraged to carry additional meals so they could offer food to people they encountered along their routes.Keeping the spirit of giving aliveMarshall’s work received further attention in a Voice of America report in December 2019, which documented the family’s continued involvement in holiday food distribution. The report showed Marshall and her sister preparing 30 turkeys for Thanksgiving, with volunteers helping organise packaging and deliveries.The operation had grown into a collective family and community effort, but its purpose remained rooted in the example set by Woodridge decades earlier. For Marshall, continuing the tradition meant ensuring that the people her mother had once served were not forgotten. Her kitchen, rather than a dedicated community centre, had become the place where that commitment was carried forward.What began as her mother’s neighbourhood initiative had evolved into a family tradition that brought food, practical support and a sense of community to hundreds of people during the holidays.You use AI every day. articles.title: UK man jailed for life after drowning ex-Microsoft executive at private members’ club in drug-fuelled murder
articles.summary: A man has been sentenced to life in prison for the brutal murder of former Microsoft executive Jennifer Symonds, whose life was tragically cut short at a private members’ club in Oxfordshire. The chilling details reveal a drug-fueled attack that ended with Symonds being drowned in the River Thames.
articles.body: A former Microsoft executive was killed after a man struck her repeatedly with a metal weight-lifting bar before holding her underwater in the River Thames at a private members’ club in Oxfordshire.Nelio Gouveia, 45, was handed a life sentence at Oxford Crown Court for killing Jennifer Symonds, 44, at Phyllis Court club in Henley-on-Thames in March. He will serve a minimum of 22 years and six months in prison, The Independent reportedThe court heard that Gouveia, who worked as a kitchen porter at the club, had arranged to meet Symonds on 5 March. They spent the evening visiting pubs and consuming alcohol and drugs before going to his room at the venue. A club member later reported hearing a man shouting “I love you”, followed by a woman screaming.The attack took place after Gouveia left Symonds near a pavilion. He visited a pornographic website before returning to his room to collect a metal weight-lifting bar. Concealing the weapon in the back of his trousers, he went back to the riverside, where Symonds was waiting.Gouveia hit her over the head three or four times, causing them to fall against a boat moored nearby and into the river, prosecutor Neil Moore told the court.He then prevented Symonds from reaching the surface, pushing her head underwater with his hands while using his feet to keep her submerged. Moore said the assault continued for approximately 12 minutes.“Jennifer Symonds fought desperately to cling on to her life,” the prosecutor said, adding that Gouveia became more determined to keep her underwater as she struggled.Gouveia pleaded guilty to the murder last month. The incident was recorded by CCTV cameras, although the footage was not played during the hearing. Mr Justice Jay described the recording as “deeply disturbing and upsetting”.The sentencing hearing also examined Gouveia’s history of violence against women. He had been given a suspended prison sentence for attacking another woman in June 2022 and was still serving that sentence when Symonds was killed. During the earlier incident, he punched the woman in the face and struck her with a wine bottle at a gathering.Mr Justice Jay said the similarities between the two assaults were “disturbing”. He described Gouveia as having a propensity for violence towards women, saying excessive drug and alcohol consumption had fuelled his behaviour during the murder.The judge also referred to Gouveia’s “appetite for violent pornography” and said the killing represented an “exercise of power and desire to dominate”. He further described the removal of some of Symonds’s clothing as an act of “humiliation and degradation”.Prosecutors raised the possibility that Gouveia attacked Symonds because she had rejected a sexual advance. However, the judge said this remained a possible explanation rather than something established to the criminal standard.Symonds had built a career in the technology industry and worked at Microsoft before being made redundant the year before her death. She was born in Zambia and moved to the UK at the age of three. After studying at the University of Gloucestershire, she went on to work in IT and received several professional awards, the court heard.Her family spoke about the loss during the proceedings. Her brother, Andrew Symonds, said she was “deeply missed every day” and remembered her as a kind and caring person who had affected the lives of many people.Her father, Peter Symonds, described the family's trauma as “devastating”. He said he continued to be haunted by what his daughter had suffered before her death and urged the judge to “please protect other women for as long as possible”.Following the murder, Gouveia travelled by taxi to Heathrow Airport, intending to fly to Latvia. He subsequently returned to Henley and went to a police station, where he told officers: “I think I hurt someone. I think I may have killed someone and I need to speak to someone quickly.”He was arrested on the day Symonds’s body was discovered in the Thames.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Two Kansas couples challenged their neighbours' 100-acre fenced deer-hunting operation over safety fears; a November 20 appeals court ruled it is a recreational preserve that needs a special zoning permit
articles.summary: A commercial deer-hunting business on a 100-acre property in Kansas cannot claim exemption from zoning rules just because it raises domesticated deer, a
articles.body: A commercial deer-hunting business on a 100-acre property in Kansas cannot claim exemption from zoning rules just because it raises domesticated deer, a state appeals court has ruled. The November 20 decision followed objections from two neighbouring couples, who raised concerns about customers using firearms and other weapons close to their homes.Danny and Laura Hawkins run the business, called OZsome Big Game Hunts. Customers pay between $3,500 and $7,500, depending on the size of the deer's antlers, for an opportunity to hunt the animals.Their neighbours, Jim and Diana Iseman and Bill and Kara Reynolds, challenged the operation. They argued that it was a commercial hunting business, not an agricultural activity, and should therefore require a special-use permit.The Hawkins maintained that they were raising domesticated deer, which are treated as livestock under Kansas law. They argued that the agricultural exemption protected their property from county zoning restrictions.The Kansas Court of Appeals upheld an earlier district court ruling that the property was being used as a recreational hunting preserve. It said the business needed a special-use permit under Coffey County's zoning rules.How the dispute beganAccording to the ruling, the matter first came before the county's zoning administrator in 2019. On July 9, the administrator sent the Hawkins information about agricultural zoning rules and an application for a special-use permit, which carried a $150 fee.After investigating the operation, the administrator informed them in a July 25 letter that the hunting preserve violated county zoning rules. The Hawkins appealed to the county's Board of Zoning Appeals.In October 2019, the board overturned the administrator's decision. It classified the property as a privately owned wildlife habitat and reserve, treating it as agricultural land that did not need a special-use permit.The neighbouring couples challenged that decision in court. In February 2021, the district court ruled in their favour, finding that the property was being used for commercial recreational hunting rather than agriculture.Why court rejected agricultural exemptionThe appeals court accepted that domesticated deer qualify as livestock and that raising them is an agricultural activity. However, it said the main purpose of the Hawkins' property was important in deciding whether the exemption applied.The business advertised hunting packages as an experience for paying customers. It also offered photography and video services, along with transport to and from Kansas City International Airport for visitors travelling from outside the state.Customers could hunt with high-powered rifles or bows and arrows. The business advertised that they could use "whatever weapon you want".The court said these services showed that customers were paying for a recreational hunting experience. The deer were specially bred and managed for that purpose, rather than being raised as part of a traditional agricultural operation.The judges also referred to earlier Kansas cases involving wildlife hunting and racehorse training. In one case, landowners who grew crops to attract wild animals were considered to be using their property for agriculture. The court said the Hawkins' operation was different because customers hunted domesticated deer kept inside a fenced area.It also drew a comparison with a case involving racehorses. Although horses are livestock, training them for racing was found to go beyond the traditional meaning of agriculture. The judges applied a similar distinction to the deer-hunting business.Neighbours' concerns about huntingThe neighbouring couples also questioned the risks of allowing customers to use weapons near their properties, which are a few hundred yards from the hunting area.The court noted that the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks does not regulate the killing of domesticated deer because they are classified as livestock. They fall under the Department of Agriculture instead. There is no designated hunting season for these deer, although state law requires hunters to hold a valid Kansas hunting licence.The judges also considered the neighbours' concern that bullets could travel beyond the fenced property. They said county rules allow certain activities to require special approval when they could affect nearby properties.Landowners' role in the earlier caseThe appeals court also considered a separate dispute over the legal proceedings. The Hawkins had not been named as parties when the neighbours first challenged the zoning board's decision, even though the case directly affected how they could use their land.The court agreed that the landowners should have been included. It found that the county's interests did not necessarily match theirs and that the Hawkins had not been adequately represented.It also upheld the district court's decision to allow them to join the case and reopen the earlier judgment, finding that they had acted within a reasonable time after learning their interests were not being properly represented.The appeals court affirmed the district court's ruling. The Hawkins' hunting business must obtain a special-use permit to operate under Coffey County's zoning regulations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Guo Wengui paid $67.5 million for a New York apartment in 2015; 11 years later, the home has reportedly sold for just $8 million to billionaire Nelson Peltz's son after bankruptcy and a major price collapse
articles.summary: A luxury apartment in Manhattan's prestigious Sherry-Netherland building has reportedly been sold for just $8 million, more than a decade after its
articles.body: A luxury apartment in Manhattan's prestigious Sherry-Netherland building has reportedly been sold for just $8 million, more than a decade after its previous owner, Chinese businessman Guo Wengui, purchased it for $67.5 million. The buyer is Diesel Peltz, the 33-year-old son of billionaire investor Nelson Peltz.According to the New York Post, Diesel completed the purchase on Wednesday, acquiring the building's entire 18th floor. The transaction marks a dramatic fall in the property's value after it was once listed for as much as $153.5 million, around $86 million above Guo's original purchase price.The apartment's asking price was gradually reduced over the years, with its final listing price standing at $12 million before the reported $8 million sale.The property was sold through a bankruptcy trustee as part of efforts to recover money owed by Guo, whose bankruptcy filing in 2022 listed approximately $374 million in debts.Property appraiser Jonathan Miller had earlier described the expected transaction as potentially the biggest recorded loss on an individual residential property sale in New York City."This will be the largest loss on an individual residential sale on record in New York City. Nothing comes close to $50 million," Miller told the New York Post when the apartment went under contract.Who is Guo Wengui and why was his apartment sold?Guo, also known as Miles Kwok and Ho Wan Kwok, is a Chinese businessman who is currently serving a 30-year prison sentence in Danbury, Connecticut.He was arrested in 2023 and charged with defrauding investors of more than $1.3 billion through various investment, media and cryptocurrency schemes. In 2024, he was convicted on nine of 12 counts, including wire fraud, racketeering and money laundering. He has maintained his innocence and appealed his conviction in July.The Manhattan apartment was held through shell companies and put up for sale by a bankruptcy trustee to help repay creditors.The property also attracted attention because of an incident in March 2023, when FBI agents arrived at the residence to arrest Guo. A fire broke out inside the apartment during the operation. Sources told the New York Post that they believed the fire may have been deliberately set off remotely and alleged that the apartment had been wired to record visitors.Guo had also used the 15-room property to livestream videos discussing alleged corruption and sensitive information about China.Luxury apartment carries hefty maintenance costsThe 7,000-square-foot apartment features an additional 2,000 square feet of outdoor space spread across three terraces. It also has a private, wood-panelled elevator providing direct access to the 18th floor.However, the property comes with substantial running costs. Monthly maintenance is approximately $85,000, with an additional $10,000 charged for the use of maids' rooms.Real estate experts said the steeply discounted sale could affect property valuations elsewhere in the prestigious building.Jenny Lenz, managing director at Dolly Lenz Real Estate, said the transaction could make prospective buyers question the value of other apartments in the building. She also pointed to the high monthly costs as a major concern for potential purchasers.However, Michael Lorber of Douglas Elliman, who represented the buyer alongside Alexander Boriskin, said the transaction demonstrated continued interest in luxury properties on Fifth Avenue."Aspirational asking prices don't define a building. Closings do," Lorber said, adding that the apartment could become one of the world's most spectacular homes after renovation.Diesel Peltz is one of the 10 children of Nelson Peltz and his third wife, former model Claudia Heffner Peltz. He is also the brother of actress Nicola Peltz, who is married to Brooklyn Beckham, son of football star David Beckham.Diesel is a co-founder of social networking app Twenty and health technology platform Healthy Together. He has also worked at his father's investment firm, Trian Partners.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump reposts ‘TrumpCare’ proposal from democrat he previously called a ‘jihadist’
articles.summary: President Trump highlights Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's 'TrumpCare' proposal, advocating for universal healthcare coverage for all Americans, signaling potential bipartisan cooperation.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has drawn attention to a universal healthcare proposal from Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed after sharing the Democrat’s mock ‘TrumpCare’ campaign on Truth Social, days after he urged the president to guarantee medical coverage for every American.Trump reposted a screenshot of El-Sayed’s November 12 post on Saturday but did not add any comment explaining his response or indicating whether he supported the proposal.El-Sayed had used images of a fictional gold card bearing the name ‘TrumpCare’ to pitch his plan, which calls for healthcare coverage for all Americans throughout their lives. Addressing Trump directly, he wrote on X: “Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”The card's design appeared to draw inspiration from Trump's $1 million Gold Card visa programme, which features the president's portrait, signature and an American bald eagle.El-Sayed, a former public health official who made Medicare for All a central part of his election campaign, is due to take office in January. His proposal comes as Trump has indicated a willingness to work with Democrats on healthcare following their gains in the midterm elections.Speaking to Fox News in a telephone interview on Saturday, Trump said there was an opportunity for both parties to make progress on healthcare, despite their differences.“They have some good points on healthcare, and they have some bad points, and we have some good things, and probably they would say we have some bad things,” Trump said, referring to congressional Democrats.“But there’s a chance we could get great healthcare and a lot of other things, and we do it in a bipartisan way,” he added.The president had expressed a similar position during a press conference on Friday, saying he was “open to great healthcare”.“There’s a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done, especially on healthcare,” Trump said. “It can be a combination of what we all want, and we could end up with great healthcare in our country. We could end up better than dealing with the Republicans.”However, his comments have come alongside warnings that he would use his presidential powers if Democrats pursue legislation he opposes.A day after the election, Trump said he was willing to work with Democrats unless they sought to be destructive, while reminding them of his ability to veto legislation.“I’ll get along, probably, with the Democrats unless they want to be destructive,” he said. “But I have the power of the veto.”During his Saturday interview, Trump also said he did not believe rejecting everything Democrats pass over the next two years would be the right approach. Later that day, he shared another image of himself on Truth Social wearing a red hat and jacket bearing the word ‘VETO’.Responding to Trump's remarks, El-Sayed said he was willing to discuss his proposal with the president if the administration was genuinely interested in working across party lines to improve healthcare access.In a statement issued on Saturday afternoon, the senator-elect said he was prepared to collaborate with other lawmakers to pursue guaranteed healthcare coverage.“If the President is serious about meeting the unmet promise of guaranteed healthcare in this country, I’m ready to work alongside leaders in the Senate like Senators Van Hollen, Sanders, Wyden, and Warren to deliver,” El-Sayed said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Why cats and rabbits hate closed doors
articles.summary: If you live with a cat or a rabbit, you already know that a shut bedroom or bathroom door is practically a personal insult.
articles.body: If you live with a cat or a rabbit, you already know that a shut bedroom or bathroom door is practically a personal insult. The moment the latch clicks, paws start scratching at the bottom gap, noses press against the wood, and thumps or meows echo down the way. It is easy to laugh off this behavior as stubbornness or separation anxiety, but both cats and rabbits have deeply rooted biological reasons for despising barriers. Even though cats are predators and rabbits are social prey animals, cats' brains and rabbits' brains are wired to treat a closed door as a direct threat to their daily survival.What happens when you close the door?Territory is everything for cats and rabbits. Both cats and rabbits are fierce creatures that rely on constant patrol routes to feel secure. In the wild, a cat survives by knowing every inch of its hunting grounds, while a rabbit survives by memorizing every escape route and burrow entrance in its warren. When you close a door inside your house, you suddenly slice their established territory in half. From their perspective, a familiar, safe zone has vanished overnight, and they are no longer able to verify that the space is free of intruders or hidden dangers.To refresh scent markersAnimals do not just look at their territory; they map it out with their noses. Cats have scent glands on their cheeks, paws, and flanks, and they spend hours rubbing against doorframes and furniture to leave a comforting chemical signature. Rabbits do the exact same thing using scent glands located directly underneath their chins. A closed door blocks them from refreshing these vital scent markers. They like to keep tabs on their favorite people, even if they just want to sleep quietly in the corner of the same room. When you shut them out, you break that passive connection and leave them wondering why they have been excluded from the group. Rabbits are deeply social animals that naturally live in large, tight-knit colonies. Being separated from their bonded partner or their human caregivers by a solid door goes directly against their natural instinct to stay close to the group for warmth and mutual protection.Simple curiosity and boredomIndoor pets live in environments that rarely change from day to day. Because their world is relatively predictable, any sudden alteration, such as a door swinging shut, immediately becomes the most interesting thing happening in the house. To a cat or a rabbit, the space behind a closed door automatically becomes a forbidden mystery. They want to investigate the smells leaking under the doorframe, check if anything new has appeared inside, and simply satisfy the urge to explore every corner of their home.How to keep the peaceSince you cannot rewrite millions of years of evolutionary wiring, the easiest solution is often just leaving interior doors slightly ajar whenever possible. If you need privacy or want to keep pets out of certain rooms for safety reasons, try distracting them before you close the latch. Tossing a handful of hay into a foraging mat for a rabbit or setting out a puzzle feeder for a cat gives their brains a rewarding task to focus on. Over time, consistent routines will teach them that a closed door is only temporary and that their territory is still completely safe.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: ‘Multi-department approach needed to curb cases’: NHM official on outreach to teenage couples in Jharkhand
articles.summary: NHM Jharkhand says multi-department action, ASHA/ANM outreach and social media counselling target teenage couples to curb rising teenage pregnancies in high-burden districts.
articles.body: Dr Pushpa, nodal officer for maternal health and family planning at the Jharkhand chapter of NHM, speaks to Dhrubajyoti Malakar about efforts by grassroots health workers in reaching out to unmarried teenage couples living together in areas reporting high teenage pregnancy rates. Excerpts:What are the reasons behind the rise in teenage pregnancies?Several factors are contributing to the rise, including school dropouts and the continued practice of child marriage in some pockets of the state. Another factor is the traditional Dhuru custom, under which teenage couples in some tribal communities live together without formally solemnising their marriage.Which districts have a higher prevalence of cases?West Singhbhum, Dumka, Deoghar, Pakur, Godda, Jamtara, Khunti and Sahibganj have reported a higher prevalence of teenage pregnancy.What are the ripple effects of teenage pregnancy?Teenage pregnancy is a factor contributing to the state’s maternal mortality burden. Many adolescent girls are already anaemic when they conceive. Whether they undergo an abortion or continue with pregnancy and childbirth, both situations can increase risks for the mother and child.What initiatives is the health department taking to address the issue?Curbing teenage pregnancy requires a coordinated approach involving the education, women and child development, and health departments, as the causes are interconnected. The health department has identified high-burden areas and directed Asha workers, sahiyas and ANMs to reach out to unmarried teenagers living together in villages. They are being counselled on family planning methods and the risks associated with early pregnancy.The department is also using social media campaigns to spread information on family planning among teenage couples living together. The aim is to provide information and support to prevent unintended pregnancies.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.
